questions.stem: A cuboid has dimensions 5 cm by 4 cm by 3 cm. What is its total surface area?
A triangular prism has a cross-section that is a right-angled triangle with legs 3 cm and 4 cm. The prism is 10 cm long. The hypotenuse is 5 cm. What is the total surface area?
questions.explanation: Two triangular faces: 2 x (1/2 x 3 x 4) = 12 cm squared. Three rectangular faces: (3 x 10) + (4 x 10) + (5 x 10) = 30 + 40 + 50 = 120 cm squared. Total = 12 + 120 = 132 cm squared.

questions.stem: A cube has surface area 150 cm squared. What is the length of each edge?
questions.explanation: A cube has 6 identical square faces. SA = 6s^2. So 150 = 6s^2, giving s^2 = 25, and s = 5 cm.

questions.stem: A cuboid has a square base of side 6 cm and a height of 10 cm. What is the total surface area?
questions.explanation: Two square faces: 2 x 6^2 = 72 cm squared. Four rectangular faces: 4 x (6 x 10) = 240 cm squared. Total = 72 + 240 = 312 cm squared.

questions.stem: A triangular prism has a cross-section that is an equilateral triangle with side 6 cm (height of triangle approximately 5.2 cm). The prism is 15 cm long. What is the total surface area to the nearest cm squared?
questions.explanation: Triangle height = (sqrt(3)/2) x 6 = 3 sqrt(3) = 5.196 cm. Two triangular faces: 2 x (1/2 x 6 x 5.196) = 31.18 cm squared. Three rectangular faces: 3 x (6 x 15) = 270 cm squared. Total = 31.18 + 270 = 301.18, approximately 301 cm squared.
